title: Later exact gate entry overrides the first matching approximate entry
description: Ledger.gate uses share 0 whenever exact_native finds any exact entry, so a later exact entry beats the first entry with epsilon <= share (§8.3): wrong answer. Witness: two h, target entries [eps .001, time 1] then [eps 0, time 100], --epsilon 0.01: estimate gives time 200, error 0; §8.3 gives time 2 (share .005, first entry matches); bennett-sched gives 2. Reproduces at HEAD d32ef4f: test_e1_first_matching_approx_entry_precedes_later_exact_entry ('200' != '2'). Probe: bennett-estimate/.tmp/opus-reviews/probe/test_probe.py (runs src/estimate.py from the review worktree at d32ef4f); run: cd .tmp/opus-reviews/probe && python3 -W ignore -m unittest test_probe. Review: docs/reviews/2026-11-02-design-review.md (E1).

title: Clarify tuple-only estimate parameters versus token identity aliasing
description: EST-CONTEXT-03: K13 encodes token parameters only by four-string tuples, while matched pairs and uncall boundary equality can depend on handle identity. The VM-admitted tests/fixtures/token-alias-source-gap.bisa (hash cda0f55ff3f299b165453ff9162b051ddf96856a799d22e09499c226bf35c011) has a 4-step completion for the same input handle and a 3-step fault for distinct handles with equal tuples under identity equality, with identical encoded args/hash. Counts are spec-derived; the installed VM cannot execute token programs yet. Known fresh mints are distinguished; ambiguous root alias comparisons fail explicitly, and conditional bounds remain available. Exact proposed alias-context schema/API text is in docs/CONTRACT_GAPS.md and queued for the spec tracker in .tmp/sol-estimate/cross-repo-beads.md per COMMON 14. Proposal unadopted; continue independent work.

description:

No reduced stand-in, disabled vectoriser, or sampled domain satisfies this bead. Consumer gate: ladder/rung-4/gate.sh (pins.json chooses the commit under test).

title: ISA 0.9 source binding needs canonical classical and implicit-length wires
description: Determining evidence: ISA 0.9 permits r = lift.add x a with a:i1 classical, while ref lift.add requires b:wire[N] and K19 admits no integer/value as a wire actual. K25 lists exact State allocations and excludes pseudo-location allocations; 3.7 says classical params are not locations/stack/frame. Similarly lift.load.i8 has implicit length 1 but its recipe requires caller-selected L and a len[L] allocation; no source rule fixes L. Exact resource and ordinal identities differ across materialisation policies. Requires normative binding decision, not guessed parameter defaults. Exact proposed text and reproducible witnesses will be in docs/CONTRACT_GAPS.md; orchestrator request queued in .tmp/sol-estimate/cross-repo-beads.md for bennett-isa-spec (read-only here). Does not narrow any north-star scope or reopen settled K12 decimal rules.
notes: Upstream source-binding decision required. Both source witnesses are admitted by the published VM with matching object hashes; parameter FB outputs correct for all four x/a combinations. Same published lift.load shape with L=1 versus L=32 gives different exact peak/occupancy. docs/CONTRACT_GAPS.md gives exact proposed normative paragraphs and a literal adapter; .tmp/sol-estimate/cross-repo-beads.md queues filing in bennett-isa-spec per COMMON rule 14. No proposed policy adopted. Blocker is the missing published trace/default, not sibling sandbox access.

title: Any finite capacity (or eps>0) forces literal loop replay
description: With finite class capacity the estimator replays loops literally instead of summarising: corpus loopmil.bisa (qloop 100000) takes 1.4 s and summary_operations 2 with capacity unbounded, 39.8 s and summary_operations 100001 with capacity 100 (re-measured at HEAD d32ef4f by .tmp/opus-reviews/tmp/e5.py; at 519b045 qloop 10^12 timed out >120 s, eps 0.1 took 94 s). Three of four published bennett-targets targets have finite capacity, so the no-materialisation aim and EST-18 fail there, blocking rung-4 estimates (cf. bennett-estimate-b8o). Review: docs/reviews/2026-11-02-design-review.md (E5).

title: Schedule bound to a foreign expansion library silently falls back to ref
description: A schedule whose bindings.expansion names library 'other' yields an estimate under the default 'ref' library. §10.1 says non-matching bindings use defaults, but also that silently changing the expansion library is not an estimate and a consumer lacking the library reports E_SCHEDULE_INFEASIBLE. Contestable; may need a spec ruling (then file it in bennett-isa-spec). Reproduces at HEAD d32ef4f: test_e6_foreign_expansion_is_infeasible_not_silent_default. Probe: bennett-estimate/.tmp/opus-reviews/probe/test_probe.py (runs src/estimate.py from the review worktree at d32ef4f); run: cd .tmp/opus-reviews/probe && python3 -W ignore -m unittest test_probe. Review: docs/reviews/2026-11-02-design-review.md (E4).

title: Embedded schedule without bindings.expansion is selected
description: §11's schedule schema requires bindings.expansion; binding_equal treats its absence as a match for ISA 0.9, so an object whose schedule omits the field is estimated (resources returned) instead of the schedule being rejected/not selected. Reproduces at HEAD d32ef4f: test_e5_schedule_without_expansion_binding_is_not_selected.
